front: Trigger: "in place," "return k," "first k elements"
back: Read/write pointers. read scans everything; write marks the next kept slot.

front: Trigger: merge two sorted lists into the first one, which has empty space at the end
back: Three pointers, fill from the BACK. Biggest goes in the last slot.

front: Trigger: "appears more than n/2 times"
back: Count it (Counter) — or Boyer–Moore voting for O(1) space.

front: Trigger: "at least h items with at least h each"
back: Sort descending, compare value to position (1-based). Or bucket count 0..n.

front: Trigger: "rotate," "circular," "wrap around"
back: Modulo: new index (i + k) % n. Reduce k %= n first.

front: Trigger: rotate in place with O(1) space
back: Three reversals: all, first k, rest (for right rotation).

front: Trigger: "best pair where one comes before the other"
back: Best-so-far scan. Track the best left-side value (e.g., min). One pass.

front: Trigger: "unlimited transactions"
back: Greedy: add every positive day-to-day difference.

front: Trigger: "can you reach the end?"
back: Track farthest reach. Stuck if i > reach.

front: Trigger: "fewest jumps" over ranges
back: Count rings (BFS levels): jumps, ring_end, farthest.

front: Trigger: "circular route, find the start"
back: Total check + reset: if total < 0 → -1; when running tank < 0, start = i + 1.

front: Trigger: "for each i, something about everything else"
back: Prefix pass + suffix pass, then combine.

front: Trigger: water or area limited by the shorter side
back: min(max_left, max_right) - height[i]

front: Trigger: two neighbor rules (left and right)
back: One sweep per direction, merge with max.

front: Trigger: "O(1) insert, delete, AND random / index access"
back: List + dict(value → index). Delete by swapping with the last element.

front: Trigger: "last word," "trailing spaces"
back: Walk backward, skip spaces. Guard i >= 0 first. (Or split()[-1].)

front: Trigger: "common prefix"
back: Column by column. Outer loop = character position. Stop at first mismatch or short word.

front: Trigger: symbol ↔ value conversion
back: Dict lookup table. Parsing: peek at next. Building: greedy biggest-first.

front: Trigger: odd layouts (zigzag, spiral)
back: Simulate with a direction flag before hunting for formulas.

front: LC 88 Merge Sorted Array — key idea, Big-O, trap
back:
• Fill from the back with p1, p2, write
  • Loop while p2 ≥ 0 (leftover nums1 is already placed)
  • O(m+n) time, O(1) space
  • Trap: forgetting leftover nums2

front: LC 27 Remove Element — key idea, Big-O
back:
• Write pointer; keep rule nums[read] != val
  • Return write
  • O(n), O(1)

front: LC 26 Remove Duplicates (sorted) — key idea
back:
• Keep if write == 0 or differs from nums[write - 1]
  • O(n), O(1)

front: LC 80 Remove Duplicates II — key idea
back:
• Keep if write < 2 or nums[read] != nums[write - 2]
  • General k: compare with nums[write - k]
  • O(n), O(1)

front: LC 169 Majority Element — three ways
back:
• Counter: O(n) time, O(n) space
  • Sort, take middle: O(n log n)
  • Boyer–Moore: O(n), O(1) — relies on guaranteed majority

front: LC 274 H-Index — key idea
back:
• Sort desc; paper i (1-based) counts if citations ≥ i
  • O(n log n). Bucket count 0..n gives O(n)

front: LC 189 Rotate Array — key idea, trap
back:
• k %= n, then reverse all / first k / rest
  • O(n), O(1)
  • Trap: nums = nums[-k:] + nums[:-k] doesn't change the caller's list

front: LC 121 Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock — key idea
back:
• Track lowest and best; best = max(best, p − lowest)
  • best starts at 0
  • O(n), O(1)

front: LC 122 Best Time II — key idea, why greedy works
back:
• Sum every positive prices[i] − prices[i−1]
  • A climb equals the sum of its steps; taking one never blocks another
  • O(n), O(1)

front: LC 55 Jump Game — key idea
back:
• reach = max(reach, i + nums[i]); return False if i > reach
  • O(n), O(1)

front: LC 45 Jump Game II — key idea
back:
• For i in 0..n−2: farthest = max(...); if i == ring_end: jumps += 1, ring_end = farthest
  • O(n), O(1). BFS by levels

front: LC 134 Gas Station — key idea, why it works
back:
• If sum(gas) < sum(cost): -1
  • Tank < 0 at i → start = i + 1, tank = 0
  • Stations between old start and failure start emptier, so they fail too
  • O(n), O(1)

front: LC 238 Product of Array Except Self — key idea
back:
• out[i] = left product × right product
  • Pass 1 left→right fills out; pass 2 right→left multiplies a running product
  • No division (zeros). O(n), O(1) extra

front: LC 42 Trapping Rain Water — key idea
back:
• water[i] = min(max_left[i], max_right[i]) − height[i]
  • Two sweeps for the maxes: O(n) time/space
  • Two-pointer version: O(1) space (Section 02)

front: LC 135 Candy — key idea
back:
• All start at 1
  • L→R: higher than left → left + 1
  • R→L: higher than right → max(own, right + 1)
  • O(n)

front: LC 380 Insert Delete GetRandom O(1) — remove steps
back:
• i = index_of[val]; last = values[-1]
  • values[i] = last; index_of[last] = i
  • values.pop(); del index_of[val]

front: LC 58 Length of Last Word — key idea
back:
• len(s.split()[-1])
  • Or: from the end, skip spaces, then count letters (guard i >= 0)

front: LC 14 Longest Common Prefix — key idea
back:
• For each column of strs[0], check every word; stop on short word or mismatch
  • O(total chars)
  • Trick: compare only min(strs) and max(strs)

front: LC 151 Reverse Words in a String — key idea
back:
• " ".join(reversed(s.split()))
  • split() drops all extra spaces
  • In-place idea: reverse all, then each word

front: LC 28 First Occurrence in a String — key idea
back:
• Try each start 0..n−m; compare until mismatch
  • O(n·m). KMP/rolling hash for O(n+m)

front: LC 13 Roman to Integer — key idea
back:
• Dict of values
  • If next symbol is bigger, subtract this one; else add
  • Last symbol always adds

front: LC 12 Integer to Roman — key idea
back: • Greedy over 13 pairs, biggest first: 1000 M, 900 CM, 500 D, 400 CD, 100 C, 90 XC, 50 L, 40 XL, 10 X, 9 IX, 5 V, 4 IV, 1 I

front: LC 6 Zigzag Conversion — key idea
back:
• One list per row; row += step; flip step at top/bottom
  • Special case: num_rows == 1 → return s

front: LC 68 Text Justification — key idea
back:
• Greedy pack while letters + (words−1) ≤ width
  • divmod(spaces, gaps): left gaps get the extra
  • Last line and single-word lines: left-justify

front: LC 283 Move Zeroes — key idea
back:
• Write pointer keeps nonzeros in order
  • Fill the tail with zeros (or swap nums[write], nums[read])
  • O(n), O(1)

front: Write the read/write pointer skeleton
back:
write = 0
for read in range(len(nums)):
    if KEEP(nums[read]):
        nums[write] = nums[read]
        write += 1
return write

front: Write Boyer–Moore voting
back:
cand, count = None, 0
for x in nums:
    if count == 0:
        cand = x
    count += 1 if x == cand else -1
return cand

front: Write a section-reverse helper
back:
def rev(a, l, r):
    while l < r:
        a[l], a[r] = a[r], a[l]
        l += 1
        r -= 1

front: Write the best-so-far scan for max rise (i < j)
back:
lowest, best = float('inf'), 0
for x in nums:
    lowest = min(lowest, x)
    best = max(best, x - lowest)
return best

front: Write the reach loop (Jump Game)
back:
reach = 0
for i, step in enumerate(nums):
    if i > reach:
        return False
    reach = max(reach, i + step)
return True

front: Write the ring-counting loop (Jump Game II)
back:
jumps = end = far = 0
for i in range(len(nums) - 1):
    far = max(far, i + nums[i])
    if i == end:
        jumps += 1
        end = far
return jumps

front: Write a prefix pass that excludes index i ("record, then include")
back:
run = IDENTITY      # 1 for product, 0 for sum, -inf for max
for i in range(n):
    out[i] = run
    run = COMBINE(run, nums[i])

front: Write the same pass right to left
back:
run = IDENTITY
for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
    out[i] = COMBINE(out[i], run)
    run = COMBINE(run, nums[i])

front: Zigzag simulation skeleton
back:
rows = [[] for _ in range(R)]
row, step = 0, 1
for ch in s:
    rows[row].append(ch)
    if row == 0: step = 1
    elif row == R - 1: step = -1
    row += step

front: Spread spaces over gaps, extra to the left
back:
base, extra = divmod(spaces, gaps)
# gap i gets base + (1 if i < extra else 0)

front: Why does nums = something inside a function not change the caller's list?
back: It rebinds the local name. Change contents instead: nums[i] = ... or nums[:] = ....

front: nums[:] = new_list — what does it do, and what's the catch?
back: Replaces the list's contents in place. Catch: building new_list costs O(n) extra space.

front: Big-O of rotating by popping/inserting at the front k times?
back: O(n·k) — each front insert shifts the list.

front: Big-O of Majority Element via sorting?
back: O(n log n) time.

front: Big-O of checking every pair for best stock profit?
back: O(n²). Fails at n = 10⁵.

front: Big-O of trying every start in Gas Station by simulation?
back: O(n²). The reset trick gives O(n).

front: Short-circuit guard for walking backward
back: while i >= 0 and s[i] == ' ': — the i >= 0 check must come first.

front: enumerate(xs, start=1) does what?
back: Gives (1, xs[0]), (2, xs[1]) ... — handy when position is 1-based (H-Index).

front: Class basics: where does object data live?
back: On self, set in __init__. Every method takes self first.

front: random.choice(x) needs x to be...
back: Indexable (list, tuple, string). Not a set.

front: divmod(17, 5)
back: (3, 2) — quotient and remainder.

front: " ".join(reversed(words)) vs words[::-1]
back: Both reverse. reversed returns an iterator; [::-1] makes a list copy. join accepts either.

front: Remove Duplicates II: why not compare with nums[read - 2]?
back: Earlier writes may have changed what's behind read. Only the kept region (write - 2) is reliable.

front: Merge Sorted Array: loop while p1 >= 0 and p2 >= 0 — what's missing?
back: Copying leftover nums2 items when nums1 runs out first.

front: Majority: > n // 2 or >= n // 2?
back: > n // 2. With n = 4, a value appearing twice is not a majority.

front: H-Index: what's the value and what's the position?
back: Value = citations. Position (1-based, after sorting desc) = the h you're testing. Mixing them is M1.

front: Rotate Array: k = 10, n = 7. What breaks if you forget k %= n?
back: Index math and reversal bounds go past the list end.

front: Stock I: why not start lowest at 0?
back: Prices are positive. Lowest would never update, so profit = max price.

front: Jump Game: "made it" check?
back: reach >= len(nums) - 1 — the LAST INDEX, not the length. (M5)

front: Jump Game II: why loop to len(nums) - 1?
back: Standing on the last index needs no more jumps. Looping to it can count one extra.

front: Product Except Self: what should the running product start at?
back: 1, not 0.

front: Candy: what goes wrong with plain assignment in the second sweep?
back: It can lower a value the first sweep required, breaking the left-neighbor rule.

front: RandomizedSet remove: what's the most common bug?
back: Forgetting to update the moved last element's index in the dict.

front: Substring search: the range of start indexes?
back: range(n - m + 1) — includes n − m. (M5)

front: Roman to Integer: the last symbol?
back: Has no next symbol. Guard i + 1 < n before peeking. (M5)

front: Zigzag: what breaks with 1 row?
back: Row 0 is also the last row, so the step logic moves to row 1, which doesn't exist: IndexError. Return s early.

front: Bug Hunt pattern: nums[write] = read
back: M1. Copies the index. Should be nums[read].
